newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil drifts aimlessly.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil drifts aimlessly.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps drifted in aimless trading late afternoon on Thursday with prices rangebound in the absence of fresh indicators, traders said.
"The market is going nowhere, trading is thin and there is no headline news to move to the market," one trader said.

March gas oil swaps were last quoted at $25.65/$25.75 per barrel, down slightly from Wednesday's $25.70/$25.80. It traded in the morning at $25.80 and $25.70 per barrel and at $25.69 at around midday, brokers said.
Traders said in the absence of fresh physical indicators, the market was rangebound and is trading within the $25.50-26.00 per barrel level.
China's recent purchase of two physical cargoes for early March is not a signal for bigger things to come as gas oil stocks there are high, they said.
Traders said Chinese purchases for March is expected to be less than half the record one million tonnes it bought in December.
Brokers said the market did not react to news of Deng Xiaoping's death but added that some players used it to talk the market down or up.
"Those who were long said the death will lead to an increase of gasoil during the funeral and those who were short said demand will drop as factories close down," one broker said.
Fuel oil swaps were steady from midday and March was last quoted at $102.25/$103.25, down about 50 cents from Wednesday.
